articles.headline: Vikings' Murray clears concussion protocol, will start vs. Bucs
articles.description: Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray has cleared the concussion protocol and will start Sunday's game at the Buccaneers, coach Kevin O'Connell announced Monday.
articles.body:
EAGAN, Minn. -- Kyler Murray will resume his role as the Minnesota Vikings' starting quarterback Sunday against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers after clearing concussion protocol, coach Kevin O'Connell said Monday.

Backup Carson Wentz helped power the Vikings' 2-0 start, but the team always planned to get Murray back on the field when he was ready. O'Connell said Murray, who signed with the Vikings this spring after seven seasons with the Arizona Cardinals, could benefit from seeing how Wentz operated the Vikings' offense.

"Carson wasn't doing crazy things," O'Connell said. "He was just protecting the football, making good decisions, making some big-time throws when he could and running the show. And I think he saw some plays get made. I think he saw our team play totally connected and complimentary of the other two phases, and what that can do for the Minnesota Vikings on a Sunday."

Murray played only 11 snaps of the Vikings' 39-22 victory over the Green Bay Packers in Week 1 before taking a hit that left him briefly motionless on the turf at U.S. Bank Stadium. His symptoms thereafter were mild enough that he participated in all three of the Vikings' practices last week on a limited basis, and the team had high confidence that he would be ready to play against the Buccaneers.

In his brief stint on the field this season, Murray threw an interception on his first pass when pressured by a free blitzer. Overall, he completed 3 of 5 passes for 18 yards while also scrambling twice for 9 yards.

"There was a third-down conversion where he sat in there [and threw] a tight completion to Justin [Jefferson]," O'Connell said. "He did use his legs and protect himself on another play. And then just going back to that [interception], that's a great example of, 'We can't compound somebody else's error.' We opened up the A-gap. That is not how we would ever play that down if we gave our offense 100 snaps. That should never happen, a 100 out of a 100. And it did on that one and then it compounded with the turnover. We haven't turned it over since, and my expectation is we're going to protect the football and play our role offensively while continuing to grow and look like the offense we know that we can become."

In other news, receiver Jauan Jennings is expected to return after missing last week because of a death in family. O'Connell also said he will be talking about options at running back after veteran Aaron Jones Sr. took 24 carries in the Vikings' 9-3 victory over the Chicago Bears.

Jones was "pretty sore" after the game, O'Connell said. Backup Jordan Mason (thumb) is on injured reserve for another three weeks and rookie sixth-round pick Demond Claiborne is not ready to carry the load. The Vikings also have veteran DeeJay Dallas, whom they signed earlier this month, on their 53-man roster. Another veteran, Jerome Ford, is on their practice squad.

articles.headline: 2026 NBA buzz: Latest free agency and trade updates
articles.description: We're tracking deals, trades and buzz across the NBA, including Pelle Larsson getting a long-term extension with the Heat.
articles.body:
NBA free agency has almost reached the end, with several players landing in new homes this offseason.

LeBron James decided to continue his historic career with the Philadelphia 76ers after months of deliberation. The Sixers also traded for Jaylen Brown this summer, turning the franchise into a true contender with two huge moves.

Meanwhile, Giannis Antetokounmpo is headed to South Beach to team up with Bam Adebayo and the Miami Heat, and the Los Angeles Lakers have been sold for the second time in 10 months.

What will happen next during this turbulent offseason?

Check back here for all the latest buzz, news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders, with the latest info at the top:

Sept. 21

Charania: Pistons, Duren at an "impasse"

Free agent center Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons are at an impasse this season and the franchise is uncertain if he will show up to next Monday's Media Day, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

"When you talk to people close to [Duren], he feels a certain way toward the Pistons' respect level for him," Charania said on NBA Today. "For him it's been all about respect, for the team it has just been about business. ... Over the course of this offseason, his offer has been been around the $180 to $190 million over five years range. And that has also included incentives like weight clauses to my understanding. And that has all played a part in this as well.

"Over the last several weeks it's kind of quiet on this front. The sides have picked up communication. And I am told right now the Pistons offer to Jalen Duren is $200 million over five years."

Duren has until Oct. 1 to sign a qualifying offer.

Hawks' Henri Veesaar out with torn ACL

The Atlanta Hawks announced that center Henri Veesaar tore his ACL during a Sept. 15 workout. He will undergo surgery in October and is expected to miss the entire 2026-27 season.

Sept. 18

Pistons, Thompson reach five-year, $155 million extension

Detroit Pistons All-Defensive forward Ausar Thompson has agreed to a five-year, $155 million rookie-scale contract extension with the franchise, sources told ESPN.

Thompson lands the fully guaranteed extension after making first-team All-Defense and finishing third in Defensive Player of the Year voting last season. The 23-year-old averaged 9.9 points, 5.7 rebounds, 3.1 assists and 0.9 blocks in 2025-26 while leading the NBA in steals per game (2.0).

articles.headline: Jayden Daniels to see specialists before Commanders form plan
articles.description: The Commanders have not established a timeline for star quarterback Jayden Daniels to return from a dislocated left elbow.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders have not established a timeline for star quarterback Jayden Daniels to return from a dislocated left elbow.

Commanders coach Dan Quinn said Monday that Daniels underwent an MRI earlier in the day and will consult with specialists over the next two days. The Commanders will formulate a plan for the third-year quarterback's recovery and return after receiving opinions from the specialists.

With Daniels sidelined, Marcus Mariota will start at quarterback Sunday against the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks.

Daniels suffered the injury on the final play of the first half in Sunday's loss to the Dallas Cowboys. It marked the second straight season that the 2023 Heisman Trophy winner dislocated the elbow in his non-throwing arm.

Daniels missed all but one game in the second half of last season after dislocating the elbow in a blowout loss to Seattle on Nov. 2. He was out for four weeks after initially suffering the injury before returning Dec. 7 against the Minnesota Vikings.

That injury occurred when Daniels used his non-throwing arm while trying to brace himself on a fall, and the same thing happened this weekend against the Cowboys. Daniels' left elbow appeared to bend the wrong way Sunday as he braced himself and threw a wild pass that was incomplete as time expired.

ESPN's John Keim and The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Saints LT Kelvin Banks to have ankle surgery, out indefinitely
articles.description: Saints left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. is out indefinitely with a high ankle sprain and needs surgery, coach Kellen Moore said Monday.
articles.body:
New Orleans Saints left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. is out indefinitely with a high ankle sprain and will undergo surgery in the next few days, coach Kellen Moore announced Monday.

Moore said the Saints would have a better idea on a timeline for Banks' return after the surgery is completed.

"So, unfortunate thing for Kelvin, but we'll just take this thing step by step and then figure out the timeline after," Moore said.

Banks almost certainly will be placed on injured reserve. Moore said there's a possibility that Banks will be able to return later this season.

Banks suffered his injury late in the third quarter of the Saints' 24-17 win against the Baltimore Ravens. Banks landed awkwardly on his ankle and stayed on the ground after the play, eventually getting into a cart and leaving the field. Asim Richards took over at left tackle for the rest of the game.

"Asim was asked to play a number of snaps last year, and he'll be asked to play a number of snaps this year. I think he's gotten better through the offseason," Moore said. "I thought he hopped in there and battled. He's gone against Trey [Hendrickson] in a couple passing situations. I thought he held his own, and so we'll prepare with him getting as many reps as he possibly can and so then he'll be ready to go."

Banks, 22, was the ninth pick of the 2025 draft and started all 17 games at left tackle for New Orleans last season. Taliese Fuaga, the Saints' 2024 first-round draft pick, started the 2024 season at left tackle but switched to right tackle last season.

articles.headline: Nicolas Batum announces retirement after 18 NBA seasons
articles.description: Nicolas Batum has announced his retirement after 18 NBA seasons. A mainstay of the French national team, Batum played most of his NBA career with the Clippers, Hornets and Blazers.
articles.body:
Nicolas Batum, a longtime NBA forward and stalwart for France's national team, announced his retirement Monday in a social media video with his son.

"Yeah, that's it," Batum said. "Dad's done playing basketball. I've been playing for a long time. ... Twenty years as a pro. That's a lot. Eighteen years in the NBA. Fifteen with the French national team. ... It's over."

Batum, 37, spent most of the past six seasons with the LA Clippers, including averaging 4.0 points and 2.5 rebounds per game in 74 appearances last season. The 2008 first-round pick entered the NBA as a teenager and spent his first seven seasons with the Portland Trail Blazers before a lengthy stint with the Charlotte Hornets and a brief stop with the Philadelphia 76ers during the 2023-24 season.

Prior to joining the NBA, Batum played two seasons in the French league.

"I decided to retire from basketball for several reasons," Batum told his 10-year-old son, Ayden, in the video. "I want to come home and be with you. I'm going to take care of you and make room for others. I think I've done my time. My time with France ended two years ago. And the NBA is over too. You know, when you've played as much basketball as I have, at some point, you have to know when to stop. ... I've done everything I needed to do."

A versatile forward capable of defending multiple positions and stretching opposing defenses with his outside shot, Batum posted career averages of 9.6 points, 4.7 rebounds and 3.0 assists per game while shooting 37.1% on 3-pointers. During his career, Batum appeared in 76 playoff games and reached the 2021 Western Conference finals with the Clippers.

The native of Lisieux, France, was deeply committed to representing his country on the international stage, competing with longtime teammates Rudy Gobert and Evan Fournier. Batum started for French teams that won silver medals at the 2020 and 2024 Olympics, he won bronze medals at the 2014 and 2019 FIBA World Cups, and he medaled at the 2011, 2013 and 2015 EuroBasket tournaments.

Batum said in the video that France's semifinal win over Germany at the 2024 Olympics in Paris was "the best basketball moment I've ever experienced."

Earlier this summer, the Clippers declined their option on Batum's $5.9 million contract for the 2026-27 season, leaving him as an unrestricted free agent.

articles.headline: Doc Rivers joins NBC as analyst, says coaching career over
articles.description: Doc Rivers turned down an offer to become an NBA analyst for NBC after retiring as a player in 1996 because he couldn't promise then-NBC Sports chairman Dick Ebersol that he wouldn't become a coach.
articles.body:
Doc Rivers turned down an offer to become an NBA analyst for NBC after retiring as a player in 1996 because he couldn't promise then-NBC Sports chairman Dick Ebersol that he wouldn't become a coach.

With Rivers now insisting that his Hall of Fame coaching career is over, the time seemed right for him to join NBC.

The network announced Monday that Rivers will be an analyst on games this season across NBC, Peacock and NBCSN, along with the possibility for some studio work.

"I honestly can say I'm absolutely retired," Rivers said in a phone interview with The Associated Press. "I had a long run. It ended up in the [Naismith] Hall of Fame [earlier this year], and I am so thankful that I was able to coach and played as long as I did. For the first time, I can focus on giving TV my 100% attention, which I'm really looking forward to.

"I think I've always been pretty honest. I've always celebrated the game in general but told the truth. I don't think anyone has ever had a problem with honesty and the way you tell the truth. There are always times where you offend people because of the truth, but I've never really worried about that."

Rivers is sixth on the NBA's career coaching list in wins (1,194) and games (2,059). In nine seasons with Boston, he led the Celtics to the NBA title in 2008 and returned to the finals two years later. Along with Boston and Orlando, Rivers coached the Los Angeles Clippers, Philadelphia and Milwaukee.

This will not mark the first time Rivers has worked with NBC. He was a studio analyst during the 2012 London Games and got to do other sports beside basketball, including handball.

"We couldn't be happier to have him back on the NBC Sports team," NBC sports executive producer and president Sam Flood said in a statement. "Having led the Celtics to the 2008 NBA title with nearly four decades of NBA experience between coaching and playing, we are excited to add another Hall of Famer to our roster."

Rivers was with Turner Sports for three years (1996-99) before beginning his coaching career with the Orlando Magic. He also had two stints with ESPN/ABC in 2003-04 and 2023. That included being on the top announcing team with Mike Breen and Doris Burke for the first couple months of the 2023-24 season before taking the Bucks job in January 2024.

"I don't take a lot of breaks in my life. I've always been around the game, and this is a way of keeping me there," Rivers said. "When you think about it, I've played, I've coached, I've been in front office, I've done TV, I've done about everything you can do in our game. And that gives me an interesting perspective, and hopefully I can share that with the viewers."

Rivers also coached five players who became NBC analysts and played against Reggie Miller, NBC's lead analyst. Rivers, a point guard, played on four teams during his 12-year career.

He coached his son Austin and Jamal Crawford with the Clippers; Grant Hill and Tracy McGrady in Orlando; and Brian Scalabrine with Boston.

articles.headline: J.K. Dobbins, RJ Harvey injured; Broncos' run game in question
articles.description: With injuries to J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey, the Denver Broncos are looking at the week ahead before determining which running back will be ready for Sunday night's game against the Los Angeles Rams.
articles.body:
ENGLEWOOD, Colo. -- Denver Broncos coach Sean Payton's back issues have flared up again, but his team's injury questions at running back may be a bigger pain this week.

J.K. Dobbins, who leads the team in carries (18) and rushing yards (72) after two games, and RJ Harvey each have hamstring injuries that make them question marks for Sunday night's game against the Los Angeles Rams.

Payton said Monday "I think there's a lot ahead of us this week in regards to who our runners are going to be.'' Rookie Jonah Coleman, who had 33 of his 39 yards rushing in Sunday's win over the Jacksonville Jaguars on the game-closing drive, could be pushed to the front of the backfield rotation.

Dobbins left Sunday's game in the third quarter with a left hamstring injury and Harvey was a game-day inactive due to a hamstring injury he suffered in the season-opening loss in Kansas City. Overall, the team has continued to search for an identity in its offense, particularly in the run game.

On one possession against the Jaguars, the Broncos faced first-and-goal from the Jacksonville 1-yard line and had three carries from Dobbins that went for no gain, no gain and a loss of a yard. The Broncos ended up with Wil Lutz kicking a 20-yard field goal.

"It wasn't anything good,'' Payton said. " ... I would say just overall a real bad possession.''

The Rams, who play the New York Giants on Monday night, surrendered 122 yards rushing to the 49ers in their season opener.

In addition to Coleman, the Broncos have running back Tyler Badie on their active roster to go with Cody Schrader on their practice squad.

articles.headline: Kylian Mbappé refuses to criticise referee despite Madrid derby 'mistakes'
articles.description: Kylian Mbappé has refused to criticise the referee in charge of Real Madrid's 2-1 derby defeat to Atlético Madrid, despite admitting that official Miguel Ángel Ortiz Arias made "mistakes" in his handling of the match.
articles.body:
Kylian Mbappé has refused to criticise the referee in charge of Real Madrid's 2-1 derby defeat to Atlético Madrid, despite admitting that official Miguel Ángel Ortiz Arias made "mistakes" in his handling of the match.

Madrid coach José Mourinho claimed on Sunday that Ortiz Arias had failed to show "two clear red cards" for rough, first-half challenges by Kang-in Lee and Cristian Romero, bringing a printout with photos of the incidents into his post-game news conference.

The result left Madrid six points behind LaLiga leaders Barcelona with just seven games played going into the international break -- with a Clásico to come at Camp Nou in October -- leaving Mourinho under pressure already in his second spell at the Bernabéu.

"I don't think I've ever been a player who talks much about referees," Mbappé told Diario AS in an interview in Switzerland, where he has agreed a new sponsorship deal with the brand On.

"I'm not going to start now. I have my own thoughts, but I'll keep them to myself... Referees are human, they make mistakes -- and those were mistakes -- but I don't want to get into that."

Romero was shown a yellow card for treading on Jude Bellingham's knee -- after a VAR check, when Bellingham had initially been cautioned for the clash -- while Lee escaped punishment for a high boot on Federico Valverde's ankle.

Atlético then went ahead in the second half at the Metropolitano through Alejandro Grimaldo's penalty after Dean Huijsen had been sent off, before Jonathan David made it 2-0, and then Antonio Rüdiger pulled a late goal back for Madrid.

It's a second defeat for Mourinho's side this season, after losing 1-0 at Real Betis earlier this month.

Atlético clapped back on Monday with three social media posts mocking Mourinho for bringing the printouts to the post-match conference. 

The first shows a printer as it releases a copy of a page with a photo of Mourinho and a caption that says: "Stop referee harassment now." 

Mourinho on Sunday brought printed-out photos of the two incidents into the press room to show journalists, before delivering a long, damning indictment of Ortiz Arias and VAR Daniel Trujillo Suárez.

"[It's] a step backwards," Mbappé said, when asked about the derby loss. "It's very tough, we wanted to win, and we knew what kind of game it would be.

"But the team gave everything, and we're moving forward, because there's still a long way to go this season, and we have to stay on the right track... We have to work, and do more. We have to put the work in."

Mbappé will now join up for international duty with France under new coach Zinedine Zidane, who was one of the forward's childhood idols.

Zidane -- who has replaced long-term boss Didier Deschamps -- was working behind-the-scenes at Madrid when Mbappé first went on trial to the Spanish capital as a youngster.
